objective: Maintain a bounded newest-first history in the original array.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: unshift and pop remain standard mutable operations.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Recent-search histories are a concrete bounded list.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Identity, capacity and repeated events transfer to state handling.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A mutable string array and nonnegative integer cap fit this lesson.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: The zero cap and repeated terms avoid modest history loss.

defects: Negative or fractional maximum values were not excluded; a negative cap could leave the revealed pop loop running forever.
A deduplicating implementation passed the old distinct-only cases.
rationale: The new contract bounds max to nonnegative integers and keeps duplicates and empty terms as distinct events. Identity is checked even for a zero cap; a longer history checks repeated removal. Existing revealed variants already satisfy this bounded domain. The hint remains direct operation guidance, so its quality is 3/5. A splice alternative is accepted for equivalent behavior rather than pretending to enforce exact syntax.

objective: Select strictly matching enumerable keys while understanding inherited-key and shadowing semantics.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Modern for-in order and strict equality remain specified.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Inherited enumeration is less common in application dictionaries, so practical utility is one.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Ownership, shadowing, identity and NaN distinctions transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The task explicitly teaches for-in rather than disguising it as own-key enumeration.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: A revealed-answer disagreement could otherwise teach incorrect ownership behavior.

defects: Reference and junior included inherited keys while senior silently required ownership.
Original tests could not distinguish Object.is from strict equality or own-only enumeration.
Input preservation, symbols and non-enumerable shadowing were unspecified.
rationale: Retain the original for-in teaching contract and explicitly include inherited enumerable string keys. Correct the senior answer and explain that own-only filtering is a different task. Executing old variants against the new public fixtures gave 11/11 reference and junior but 9/11 senior. New cases include prototype shadowing, non-enumerable suppression, integer-key order, NaN, signed zero and reference equality. The cost model counts inspected property names and prototype objects.

objective: Invert own enumerable string entries into a safe dictionary with a defined collision rule.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Object.hasOwn, null-prototype dictionaries and fromEntries are current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Reverse lookup dictionaries have practical uses.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Ownership, property-name conversion and collision order transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Primitive string or finite-number values keep conversion explicit.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Special-key handling prevents silent missing entries and inherited-data leakage.

defects: Reference and junior disagreed with the own-only senior on inherited keys.
All old variants lost a __proto__ output key through an inherited setter.
The old hint supplied the complete assignment without teaching ownership or key collisions.
rationale: Specify own enumerable string inputs, bounded conversion cost units and last-in-Object.keys-order collisions. Loop-based reference and junior use null-prototype dictionaries and ownership checks; senior fromEntries defines data keys directly. Old variants passed only 8/10, 8/10 and 9/10 new public cases. New fixtures exercise inherited exclusions, special names, numeric zero conversion, frozen/null-prototype inputs and fresh-empty results. This is a correctness finding in an exercise, not a claimed production exploit.

objective: Merge shallow own settings with defaults using presence rather than truthiness or prototype membership.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Own-property checks and explicit dictionary objects remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Configuration defaults are common application work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Missing versus undefined, shallow identity and ownership transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A string-keyed data-object scope avoids unrelated accessor behavior.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Inherited blockers and special names can silently discard requested defaults.

defects: Using in on a normal result incorrectly blocked defaults such as toString or __proto__.
Reference and junior included inherited entries unlike senior.
Original tests did not preserve an explicitly undefined setting or nested identity.
The original hint recommended the problematic in check.
rationale: Define only own enumerable string settings/defaults and preserve explicitly present undefined, null and falsy values. Null-prototype loop answers and fromEntries avoid inherited setters while keeping shallow references. Old answers scored 8/10, 8/10 and 9/10 against new public fixtures. New tests cover ordinary reserved-looking names, inherited/non-enumerable exclusion, frozen inputs and fresh results; the misleading hint and skeleton are replaced.
